descriptions.text: Attacker manipulated the wGOOGLx collateral price, which is derived from its underlying GOOGLx balance, allowing them to borrow against the inflated collateral and drain approximately $353K. Stolen assets were swapped for 224 ETH and deposited into Tornado Cash. Source: https://twitter.com/CyversAlerts/status/2072259516435939780

Edel Finance lending protocol was exploited via wGOOGLx wrapped token exchange rate manipulation. The attacker used flash loans in repeated deposit/borrow loops to inflate wGOOGLx collateral value ~78x, then borrowed assets, creating ~$403K bad debt.

Edel Finance suffered a $403,000 loss on Ethereum after an attacker manipulated the wGOOGLx wrapper exchange rate, inflating collateral value by about 78× using flash loans. The lending protocol was left with bad debt, and funds were moved to Tornado Cash. Edel Finance relied on an internal wrapper exchange rate (wGOOGLx/GOOGLx) that was manipulable by flash-loan cycles. The protocol did not constrain rapid exchange-rate changes or validate the backing behind collateral valuation. Chainlink price feeds remained correct, but the ERC-4626 vault's assets-per-share ratio was vulnerable.
